analysis:
Examined the docs/reference/configuration.md changes and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump. In configuration.md, head line 3 changes the date, and head line 313 adds DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL. That flag is default-on; an exact 0 disables it. It is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents. It changes full-attention prefill from 128-query blocks to one fused .causal SDPA call, except for live packed paged KV. This is a performance/dispatch change. The documentation does not describe any change to the encryption, attestation, cache-scoping, or authorization controls in TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 or T-041. The other visible lines, 312 and 314-597, are unchanged context per the complete range map.

The submodule moves from 19634dd8 to fd17d026, which presumably implements the fused causal prefill in AttentionV1.swift. The submodule source was not supplied, so its correctness is unverified. That matters for:
- T-007/T-056: output correctness. A wrong causal mask could leak future tokens or produce manipulated outputs. This is a correctness rather than confidentiality issue, since everything stays within one request.
- T-028/T-041: KV and prefix-cache contents. A fused kernel that writes KV differently could affect cache adoption parity.
- Availability and memory: transient attention memory for long prompt chunks, with OOM/DoS risk under TB-007 memory admission.

The submodule bump may also include other unreviewed changes (range_map_complete=false for the submodule). No concrete regression is evidenced from the supplied text. Integration or a deeper review should inspect the mlx-swift-lm diff between 19634dd8 and fd17d026, especially:
- CBv2AttentionV1.usesFusedCausalPrefill eligibility, including the paged KV exclusion;
- causal-mask correctness for prefix-offset chunks after cache restore;
- memory admission accounting for the fused SDPA scratch.
